objective_text: Describe the purpose of Microsoft Purview in Azure
stem: A company has data in Azure, in on-premises databases and in other clouds. It wants one unified view of that data, with automated discovery and sensitive data classification. Which service fits?
why_correct: Microsoft Purview gives a single unified view of data across on-premises, multicloud and software-as-a-service sources, with automated discovery and sensitive data classification.
why_a_wrong: Azure Policy enforces rules on resource configurations, and it does not map or classify data.
why_b_wrong: Resource locks stop resources from being accidentally deleted or changed, and they do not classify data.
why_d_wrong: A policy initiative groups related policies to track compliance, and it does not discover or classify data.
author: yego

objective_text: Describe the purpose of Microsoft Purview in Azure
stem: Which task is a typical use of Microsoft Purview?
option_a: Stopping a resource group from being deleted
option_b: Requiring new resources to carry an AppName tag
option_c: Allowing only certain virtual machine sizes
option_d: Finding where sensitive data is stored across the data estate
why_correct: Purview helps identify where sensitive data is stored in your data estate, and it provides data classification and lineage.
why_a_wrong: Stopping deletion is the job of a resource lock, not Purview.
why_b_wrong: Requiring tags is something Azure Policy can do, not Purview.
why_c_wrong: Limiting virtual machine sizes is something Azure Policy can do, not Purview.
author: yego

objective_text: Describe the purpose of Azure Policy
stem: A company wants virtual machines in its subscription to be created only in approved sizes, and it also wants the existing machines checked. Which service should it use?
why_correct: Azure Policy can define a rule that allows only certain virtual machine sizes. It applies when a VM is created or resized, and it also evaluates VMs that already exist.
why_b_wrong: Purview is a data governance service and does not control virtual machine sizes.
why_c_wrong: A resource lock prevents accidental deletion or changes, and it does not set rules for allowed sizes.
why_d_wrong: A budget sets a spending limit and alerts, and it does not control which sizes are allowed.
author: yego

objective_text: Describe the purpose of Azure Policy
stem: What is an Azure Policy initiative?
option_a: A lock that stops a resource from being deleted
option_b: A group of related policy definitions used to track compliance with a larger goal
option_c: A tool that classifies sensitive data
option_d: A single policy that can only be applied to one resource
why_correct: An initiative groups related policies together so you can track your compliance state for a larger goal.
why_a_wrong: A lock that stops deletion is a resource lock, not a policy initiative.
why_c_wrong: Classifying sensitive data is a Purview capability, not an initiative.
why_d_wrong: Policies can be set at the resource, resource group or subscription level, and an initiative is a group of policies rather than a single one.
author: yego

objective_text: Describe the purpose of resource locks
stem: A critical storage account must not be accidentally deleted, but authorized users still need to read and change it. Which option fits?
why_correct: With a Delete lock, authorized users can still read and modify the resource, but they cannot delete it.
why_a_wrong: A ReadOnly lock would also stop users from updating the resource, so they could not change it.
why_b_wrong: An initiative groups policies to track compliance and does not stop a resource from being deleted.
why_c_wrong: Purview is a data governance solution and does not protect a resource from deletion.
author: yego

objective_text: Describe the purpose of resource locks
stem: An owner of a locked resource wants to change it. What must happen first?
option_a: Nothing because owners can bypass locks
option_c: Remove the lock and then make the change
option_d: Ask Microsoft Purview to approve the change
why_correct: To modify a locked resource you must first remove the lock, and then you can perform any action you have permission for.
why_a_wrong: Locks apply regardless of role-based access permissions, so even an owner cannot bypass them.
why_b_wrong: Adding another lock does not allow changes, because the lock has to be removed first.
why_d_wrong: Purview is a data governance solution and is not used to approve changes to locked resources.
author: yego
